Background The effects of a multi-ingredient performance supplement (MIPS) on markers of inflammation and muscle damage, perceived soreness and lower limb performance are unknown in endurance-trained female athletes. The purpose of this study was to determine the impact of MIPS (NO-Shotgun®) pre-loaded 4 weeks prior to a single-bout of downhill running (DHR) on hsC-Reactive Protein (hsCRP), interleukin (IL)-6, creatine kinase (CK), muscle soreness, lower limb circumferences and performance. Method Trained female runners ( n = 8; 29 ± 5.9 years) (VO 2max : ≥ 50 ml -1 .kg -1 .min -1 , midfollicular phase (7-11 days post-menses) were randomly assigned in a double-blind manner into two groups: MIPS ( n = 4) ingested one serving of NO Shotgun daily for 28 days prior to DHR and 30 min prior to all post-testing visits; Control (CON) ( n = 4) consumed an isocaloric maltodextrin placebo in an identical manner to MIPS. hsCRP, IL-6, CK, perceived soreness, limb circumferences, and performance measures (flexibility, squat jump peak power) were tested on 5 occasions; immediately before (PRE), immediately post-DHR, 24, 48 and 72 h post-DHR. Results There were main effects of time for CK ( p = 0.05), pain pressure threshold (right tibialis anterior ( p = 0.010), right biceps femoris ( p = 0.01), and left iliotibial band (ITB) ( p = 0.05) across all time points), and maximum squat jump power ( p = 0.04). Compared with 24 h post-DHR, maximum squat jump power was significantly lower at 48 h post-DHR ( p = 0.05). Lower body perceived soreness was significantly increased at 24 h ( p = 0.02) and baseline to 48 h ( p = 0.02) post DHR. IL-6 peaked immediately post-DHR ( p = 0.03) and hsCRP peaked at 24 h post-DHR ( p = 0.06). Calculation of effect sizes indicated a moderate attenuation of hsCRP in MIPS at 72 h post-DHR. Conclusions Consumption of MIPS for 4 weeks prior to a single bout of DHR attenuated inflammation three days post, but did not affect perceived soreness and muscle damage markers in endurance trained female runners following a single bout of DHR. Keywords Eccentric exercise Muscle soreness Recovery issue-copyright-statement © The Author(s) 2016 Background Exhaustive or unaccustomed high-intensity exercise [ 1 , 2 ] or eccentric contractions [ 3 , 4 ] are known to inflict muscle damage. This leads to increased muscle soreness, decreased muscle strength, increased concentration of plasma muscle enzymes, and decreased range of motion [ 1 , 2 , 4 ], for several days post exercise, and further promotes an unbalanced ratio of protein breakdown to protein synthesis [ 5 ]. A level of muscle discomfort related to the exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD), otherwise known as delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS), increases until subsiding five to seven days post-exercise [ 6 ]. Downhill running (DHR) is commonly used to induce muscle damage [ 7 ], as it involves greater eccentric contraction of the knee extensors, leading to more tissue damage, compared with level or uphill running [ 8 , 9 ]. Although similar decrements associated with EIMD have been reported in both males and females, it has been documented that females are susceptible to longer periods of recovery when compared to males; however, reasons for this are unclear [ 10 ]. However, contrary to this, estrogen appears to have a protective effect with regards to DOMS [ 11 ], as it has been reported that estrogen results in significant decreases in serum creatine kinase (CK) activities post-exercise or post-injury when compare to men or a placebo [ 12 , 13 ]. It has therefore been hypothesized that several of the sex-related differences are attributed to the female sex hormone 17β-estradiol [ 14 , 15 ]; such that estrogen has been reported to possess the ability to enhance skeletal muscle growth, gene expression, metabolism, contraction characteristics, and maintain muscle mass. Numerous studies have examined the effects of nutritional supplementation interventions to reduce the effects of EIMD by increasing the net protein balance within skeletal muscle. These studies have included supplementation with whey protein isolate [ 5 , 16 ], branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs: leucine, isoleucine, and valine) [ 17 , 18 ], protein hydrolysates [ 19 ], leucine only [ 20 ], creatine [ 21 ]; increasing anti-inflammatory and anti-oxidant activity through tart cherry juice [ 22 , 23 ], blueberry [ 24 ] and caffeine ingestion [ 25 ], as well as enhancing recovery through the consumption of chocolate milk [ 26 , 27 ] to name a few. The majority of studies investigating the ergogenic effects of nutritional supplementation on exercise performance and recovery have primarily focused on males [ 20 , 28 , 29 ]. However, there are a few studies that examined female rats and other animals, and female humans [ 30 , 31 ]. Recent studies have investigated the effects of a multi-ingredient performance supplement (MIPS; NO Shotgun®) following a single bout of DHR in trained males [ 32 ] as well as in resistance trained males [ 33 ]. However, there is little known about the effects of this MIPS on the reduction of muscle damage and repair after EIMD from DHR in endurance-trained female athletes. We hypothesized that 4 weeks of pre-loading with a MIPS prior to a single bout of DHR would decrease perceived soreness and circumferences, enhance flexibility, and improve biochemical markers of muscle damage and inflammation (i.e. CK, IL-6 and CRP), and improve squat jump performance when compared to an isocaloric placebo (CON) in endurance-trained female runners for up to 72 h post-DHR.

core_effect_and_quantification.activity_context: Multi-ingredient performance supplement (MIPS) pre-loading prior to downhill running (DHR)
core_effect_and_quantification.magnitude_quantification: Moderately attenuated in the MIPS group at 72 h post-DHR (-38.89% of baseline, moderate effect size) compared to control.

molecular_mechanism_and_relationship.activity_type_context: Exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD) from downhill running (DHR) and the effects of multi-ingredient performance supplement (MIPS) consumption on associated inflammation.
molecular_mechanism_and_relationship.mechanism_description: Downhill running (DHR) involves significant eccentric contraction of knee extensors, causing tissue damage, increased muscle soreness (DOMS, peaking 24-72h post-exercise), decreased muscle strength, elevated plasma muscle enzymes, reduced range of motion, and an imbalance in protein turnover. This also induces inflammation, indicated by changes in serum markers like creatine kinase (CK), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP). The increase in IL-6 is thought to stimulate hepatic CRP production, although their temporal peaks post-DHR (IL-6 immediately, hsCRP later) suggest a complex interplay. Estrogen is hypothesized to have a protective effect, potentially by reducing serum CK activity post-exercise/injury and supporting skeletal muscle growth and maintenance.

dose_intensity_and_specificity.dose_comparison_summary: The study involved pre-loading one serving (21g) of a multi-ingredient performance supplement (MIPS) daily for 4 weeks (28 days) prior to a single bout of downhill running (DHR), and 30 minutes prior to all post-testing visits. This regimen was compared against an identically administered isocaloric maltodextrin placebo (28g daily for 4 weeks). No varying doses of MIPS were compared. While MIPS moderately attenuated hsCRP at 72 h post-DHR, no significant treatment effects were observed for perceived soreness, muscle damage markers (CK Log), other inflammatory markers (IL-6), performance decrements, lower limb circumferences, hamstring flexibility, treadmill speed, heart rate, RPE, or overall energy intake between the MIPS and placebo groups.
dose_intensity_and_specificity.specificity_finding: The multi-ingredient performance supplement (MIPS) specifically attenuated inflammation (hsCRP) at 72 h post-downhill running (DHR), with MIPS showing a moderate decrease and the control group showing a moderate increase. However, MIPS did not significantly affect perceived soreness or other muscle damage markers. DHR is a specific model for muscle damage due to its emphasis on eccentric contractions of knee extensors. While females are often reported to have longer EIMD recovery, estrogen may offer some protection against DOMS by reducing CK. Interestingly, the study suggested that responses for perceived muscle soreness, muscle damage markers, and recovery post-DHR might be similar between well-trained males and females, indicating a potential lack of sex-specific variation in these particular responses.

clinical_implication_and_population.target_population: Eight healthy, endurance-trained female runners (29 ± 5.9 years, aged 18-40, VO2max ≥ 50 ml·kg-1·min-1, averaging 32 km·wk-1 running) from Durban, South Africa. Participants were studied during their midfollicular phase (7-11 days post-menses), and excluded if they had existing diseases, musculoskeletal disorders, leg injuries, or used anti-inflammatory drugs. A four-week washout period for other supplements was observed prior to the study.
clinical_implication_and_population.health_implication: The downhill running protocol consistently induces exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD), leading to increased muscle soreness, tissue tenderness, decrements in peak power, and elevated serum markers of muscle damage (CK) and inflammation (IL-6, hsCRP). While 4 weeks of multi-ingredient performance supplement (MIPS) consumption did not significantly attenuate perceived soreness, muscle damage markers, or overall performance decrements, it did show a potential benefit in attenuating post-exercise inflammation (hsCRP) at 72 hours post-DHR in endurance-trained female runners. This suggests a nuanced role for MIPS in exercise recovery, primarily affecting inflammatory markers rather than direct muscle damage or soreness in this population.
clinical_implication_and_population.risk_classification: Primarily an evaluation of recovery management and performance optimization, indicating a potential protective benefit against post-exercise inflammation, but also highlighting the physiological response of exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD) to acute strenuous exercise.

biomarker_reliability_and_future_focus.reliability_assessment: The study was limited by low statistical power due to a modest sample size (n=8), impacting the significance of comparisons. While no explicit assessment of reliability, sensitivity, or specificity was provided for all biomarkers, Creatine Kinase (CK) required natural logarithm transformation for statistical normality. Effect sizes for peak power were unclear, while CK and IL-6 showed a range from small to very large increases. hsCRP showed contrasting effect sizes between groups at 72 h post-DHR. The variability in muscle damage indicator responses (CK, IL-6) persists, and the indirect markers used may have had restricted sensitivity. Additionally, the small sample size made it difficult to adequately control for menstrual cycle phase and contraceptive use, which could have influenced results.
recommended_alternatives: Unbiased method to determine the degree of muscle adaptation
